title: Chocolate Chess Pie
summary: A fudgy, brownie-like chocolate filling with a shiny crackled top, baked in a part-baked butter crust.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
double cream, whipped softly, to serve

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt, bind with iced water and rest the wrapped disc in the fridge for 1 hour.

steps.title: Part-bake the case
steps.text: Line the dish with the rolled dough, crimp and chill 30 minutes. Bake with paper and beans at 190 °C (170 °C fan) for 18 minutes, then remove them and bake 5 minutes to dry the base. Lower the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan).

steps.title: Melt
steps.text: Melt the butter and chocolate together in the small saucepan over a very low heat, stirring, then let it cool for 5 minutes so it does not scramble the eggs.

steps.title: Whisk the filling
steps.text: Whisk the sugar, cocoa and salt into the chocolate, then add the eggs and vanilla and whisk just until smooth and shiny.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Pour into the warm case on a baking tray and bake 30-35 minutes, until the top is crackly and puffed and the centre jiggles a little. It firms up as it cools, so take it out before it looks fully set.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack, at least 2 hours, then slice and serve with softly whipped cream.

tips: Whisk the eggs in just until smooth; beating in air makes the top puff and sink.
A common mistake is waiting for the centre to firm up in the oven, which turns the filling dry and cakey.
Use a chocolate you like eating; its flavour carries the whole pie.
A pinch more salt sharpens the chocolate if your bar is very sweet.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at cool room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 4 days.
